MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  October 6, 2025

Vice Chair Rosoff called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez,
Vice Chair Rosoff and Commissioner Greenidge. Also, present was Rita Ruiz, Interim
Director, Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst, Marissa Velez, Office Assistant II.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Apodaca motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on September 8, 2025. Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez seconded the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins,
  Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, and Commissioner Greenidge
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Chair LeGaspi
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

OTS Grant Update

Mrs. Lomas introduced Public Safety Interim Director Rita Ruiz, who presented an update
on the OTS Grant Update. On August 19, 2025, Presented Resolution No 25-36 Budget
Amendment Grant Funding for the California Office of Traffic Safety Award. On July 9,
2025, Public Safety OEM Team applied for a Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program
Grant the City was Awarded 100,000.00. The grant is a part of a statewide effort to reduce
traffic-related injuries and fatalities. The program supports the city’s commitment to
improving pedestrian and bicycle safety. Staff recommended that the city council adopt
Resolution No. 25.36 authorizing the amendment to fiscal year 25/26 adopted budget.

Community Outreach Efforts:
  • Collaborate with Target
  • School Outreach
  o Presentations On Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety
  o Senior Center
  o Elementaries, Middle and High Schools

  •  National Night Out:
   o Bike Rodeo
  o Bike Safety Gear Giveaway

STAFF COMMENTS

Interim Director Rita Ruiz reported that the Commission’s draft mission and vision
statements, along with recommendations, have been compiled based on prior feedback.
Mrs. Lomas will follow up after the meeting with the draft for review and further input.

Policy and Procedure

Minimum Requirements and Duties of Commissioner

  •  Promote greater public awareness for security and safety of all citizens in
  Norwalk.
  •  Provide educational opportunities for residents in developing a high level of
  protective concern and awareness for the community.
  •  Hear and decide matters relating to installation of disabled person’s parking
  zones in the public right-of-way throughout the city.
  •  Respond to requests on security and public safety hazards and prepare related
  fact-finding reports and resulting recommendations.
  •  Recommend to City Council, after public input, the adoption, amendment or
  repeal of ordinances or resolutions affecting public safety, and parking municipal
  codes affecting the public right-of-way, in the City of Norwalk.
  •  Acquire information related to the above responsibilities, which may include
  attendance at professional seminars or workshops.
  •  The Commission shall not serve as any type of review board monitoring the
  actions of the Sheriff’s Department or its officers or personnel.

Vision Statement:

The Public Safety Commission is dedicated to fostering a safe, informed, and engaged
community by working in partnership with residents, City leaders, Public Safety Officers,
we are committed to transparency, ethical conduct, and professional representation in
all that we do.

Mission Statement:

Educate and involve residents in understanding the role of Public Safety and the Los
Angeles Sheriff’s Department.
Support law enforcement and City initiatives through active participation in community
events, outreach programs, and public engagement opportunities.
Uphold accountability and professionalism by maintaining consistent attendance, ethical
training, and visible representation at City meetings and events.
 Serve with dedication, loyalty, and honesty to strengthen trust between the city, Public
Safety personnel, and the community we represent.
Together, we strive to be visible, approachable, and committed partners in ensuring the
well-being of Norwalk and its residents.

Department Monthly Update:

Mrs. Lomas reviewed the 2025 Monthly Calendar and highlighted October as National
Emergency Awareness Month. Interim Director Ruiz shared that the department
launched a “What’s in Your Go Bag?” and shared the contest winners on our Public
Safety Monthly Recap video.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez inquired about the date for National Night Out. Interim Public
Safety Direct advised that National Night Out is the first week of August. We are in the
planning stages and hope to change it from previous years and add the Bike Rodeo.

Vice Chair Rosoff and Commissioner Apodaca inquired about the Red Ribbon Ceremony
at the Lowes. Public Safety Interim Director and staff confirmed the time was 10:00 am
and for a billboard near the store.

Commissioner Greenidge inquired about faded red curbs and process of having curbs
repainted and replacement of faded or covered street signs. Interim Director Rita Ruiz
advised that she speak to Commissioner Greenidge after the meeting on the process
work order request system.

Commissioner Apodaca inquired and confirmed that she will be attending the First
Responder Luncheon. Mrs. Lomas Confirmed receiving RSVP for all attending
commissioners.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:17 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
